lines.text: Organizations for your health [gezondheid]:
The Municipal Health Service [GGD, Gemeentelijke Gezondheidsdienst] protects people's health and belongs to the municipality.
You can get vaccinations [vaccinaties] there; the child health clinic [consultatiebureau] is also part of the GGD.
Social work [Maatschappelijk werk] helps with problems such as relationship problems, problems at work or loneliness [eenzaamheid].
You can contact them yourself or get a referral [verwijzing] from your GP.
Health insurers reimburse [vergoeden] sessions with social work.
Organizations for financial problems [financiële problemen]:
The National Institute for Budget Information [Nibud, Nationaal Instituut voor Budgetvoorlichting] helps with financial advice or financial problems.
With debts [schulden] the municipality can help; there are also organizations for debt assistance [schuldhulpverlening].
In every larger town there is a food bank [voedselbank] or clothing bank [kledingbank]: free food or clothing for people with a low income.

Legal help [Juridische hulp]: at the legal aid desk [Juridisch Loket] you can ask questions about your rights and duties, for example with problems with your residence permit, a complaint [klacht] against the government, a divorce, or punishment.
It is free if you have a low income.
For a court case with a lawyer [advocaat] you pay part of the costs yourself — with a low income that is not much.
For refugees there are organizations such as Vluchtelingenwerk.
People who work for the government must follow rules.
They may not ask for money or anything else in return when they do something for someone — that is called corruption [corruptie] and it is forbidden [verboden].
Discrimination is also forbidden, not only for the government but also for other institutions, such as your school, your landlord [huisbaas] or the hospital.
Complaints against the government or other institutions [Klachten tegen de overheid of andere instanties]: if you feel you have been badly treated [behandeld], you can object:
First submit [indienen] a complaint yourself.
Does that not help?

Then you can go to an ombudsman: the municipal ombudsman [gemeentelijke ombudsman] for complaints against the municipality, the Nationale ombudsman for other complaints, for example about the Belastingdienst.
The ombudsman can help you free of charge [gratis].
The Juridisch Loket can also help.
Organizations must have a complaints committee [klachtencommissie] and confidential advisers [vertrouwenspersonen].
If necessary, you can file a report with the police.
There are also reporting points [meldpunten] to report discrimination.
